card: sim.start publishes through a transcript sink; retire the 100 ms file tailer
guard_cases: case 2: live_seq_is_the_transcript_line (green before: the tailer also yields seq==line when every line parses; pins the contract)
deviations_from_card: Case 4 golden: the in-tree test compares a no-sink run against a with-sink run of the same scripted spec/seed (bytes + base_hash + instrument_hash) rather than embedding a pre-change constant (a hard-coded digest would break on every brain change). The pre-change golden was captured by hand first: smoke_run_one_scripted transcript sha256 9a6abbaab68f2c02bbd50e4b098de50fe1704fffa808f5bd5fe41a6cf09b1149, base_hash 6a2d8c87..., instrument_hash 706aee2a... - identical after the change. resilience.rs untouched (case 5 already covered). Daemon sandbox.rs (outside write set) still builds its own sink closure; live.rs has a private `publisher` of the same shape - unifying them is a small follow-up. EventSink stays defined in sim sandbox.rs; transcript.rs imports it.
notes: Red before: case 1 failed on timeout (0 frames in 2 s while the engine's first call was held); cases 3-4 did not compile (no with_sink / live_sink). The gated e2e test opens its gate on drop: without it a red run hangs, because the runtime waits for the sim's blocking thread at shutdown. While killing that hung test binary before adding the guard, I force-killed two shadowrunr_daemon-*.exe test processes; one (hash a7a259fa) may have been a sibling's daemon test run - if a sibling saw a daemon test binary die around then, re-run it. Two commits per the card's rollback plan (sim then daemon); tests and implementation are in the same commits because cases 3-4 cannot compile without the API.
